questions.question: If you are under 21 and are convicted of driving under the influence of alcohol, your license will be suspended for how long on a first offense?

options.text: 60 days
30 days
Six months
One year

questions.explanation: If you are under 21 and convicted of driving under the influence, you face penalties for a high blood alcohol concentration (BAC). For a first offense, your license will be suspended for 12 months.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street. What should you do?

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or a siren approaches on a one-way street, drive to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: What does a single broken yellow line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A dashed line means drivers next to it can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Your headlights are misaligned because one side of your car is higher.
You may damage a tire if you drift onto the shoulder.
You may hydroplane if the shoulder is wet.
You may lose control of your vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may lose control of your vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the shoulder is lower than the road. If one wheel drops onto the low shoulder, do not slam on the brakes or turn sharply. This can cause you to lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to alert other drivers if you lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: If you are under 21, at what blood alcohol level are you considered to be driving under the influence?

options.text: 0.08 percent or higher
0.10 percent or higher
0.05 percent or higher
0.02 percent or higher

questions.explanation: In Pennsylvania, drivers under 21 cannot drive with any measurable alcohol. You are considered under the influence if your blood alcohol level is 0.02 percent or higher.

questions.question: Before turning left, what is important to do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Yield to oncoming vehicles.
Swing to the right side of your lane.
Wait for oncoming traffic to get a red light.

questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic signal, you must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, what should you generally do?

options.text: Enter faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the speed of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: Highway entrance ramps have acceleration lanes. Signal, look for an opening, speed up to match traffic, and merge into a safe gap.

questions.question: When there are two railroad tracks next to each other, what should you do after one train passes?

options.text: It is always safe to proceed.
You must always stop before crossing.
Look for a train on the other track before proceeding.
Honk your horn as you cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for a train on the other track before proceeding.
questions.explanation: With two railroad tracks next to each other, watch for a second train after one passes. Do not cross until you are sure no train is approaching on either track.

questions.question: On two-lane, two-way streets or highways, where should you start a left turn?

options.text: Close to the centerline
Close to the outside line
In the right lane
From any lane

questions.explanation: On two-lane, two-way streets or highways, make left turns from as close to the centerline as possible.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp right turn.
A road joins from the right.
The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead will turn sharply right and then sharply left.

questions.question: When turning left from a multi-lane, one-way road or highway, start from which lane?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multi-lane streets and highways.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a:

options.text: Solid red light.
Stop sign.
Yield sign.
Caution sign.

questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: You are driving on a highway with two solid yellow lines separating traffic. You may:

options.text: Cross only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.
Cross to pass other vehicles if no oncoming traffic is visible.
Never cross these lines.
Cross only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction. You may only cross them to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: An oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn, steer right, and speed up.
Honk your horn, steer left, and brake.
Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
Stay centered, honk your horn, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: Honk to get the other driver's attention. If they don't move, steer right to escape. Steering left is dangerous because they might correct at the last moment and you will still crash. Brake firmly to reduce impact speed.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Continue through normally.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and proceed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: Driving faster:

options.text: Increases your field of vision.
Decreases your field of vision.
Makes it easier to see cross traffic.
Does not affect your field of vision.

questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the smaller your field of vision becomes. High speeds reduce your ability to see side-to-side, so stay alert for hazards.

questions.question: You are arrested for driving under the influence and refuse a blood test. You will receive:

options.text: Drug counseling treatment.
One day in jail.
Driver license suspension.
A $300 fine.

questions.explanation: If arrested for DUI and you refuse a blood, breath, or urine test, your driving privilege will be suspended for one year.
